original_question: Characterize exactly which graphs admit a unit bar visibility representation, meaning a bar visibility representation in which all horizontal bars have the same length.
target_in_paper: Section 3.3, Open Problem 17: "Characterize unit bar visibility graphs."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the paper's characterization problem for unit bar visibility graphs, and it correctly captures the defining extra restriction that all horizontal bars in the representation have the same length.
missing_details: The geometric model is implicit: each vertex must correspond to a horizontal bar (line segment) in the plane, and the bars are pairwise disjoint.
The adjacency rule is implicit: two vertices are adjacent exactly when their corresponding bars have an unobstructed vertical line of sight between them.
The paper phrases the problem as a characterization of the graph class of unit bar visibility graphs, not as an algorithmic recognition problem for a given input graph.
The draft does not explicitly separate this target from the neighboring Open Problem 18, which asks about NP-completeness of recognition rather than characterization.
refined_question: Determine necessary and sufficient conditions for a graph G to be a unit bar visibility graph; that is, for G to admit a bar visibility representation by pairwise disjoint horizontal bars in the plane, one for each vertex of G, such that uv is an edge of G if and only if the bars for u and v have an unobstructed vertical line of sight between them, with the additional restriction that all bars have the same length.
justification: This draft matches the paper's Section 3.3 discussion of bar visibility graphs. The paper first defines bar visibility graphs using disjoint horizontal bars and unobstructed vertical visibility, then immediately introduces unit bar visibility graphs by imposing the equal-length condition on all bars, and the next numbered statement is Open Problem 17, "Characterize unit bar visibility graphs." The adjacent Open Problem 18 is a different question about recognition complexity, so the refined version should stay narrowly on characterization.
